adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 — event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match — permanently dead lookup that reads as intentional.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (updateEvent), the code computes:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `undefined`/`null`/""), so it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value. In normal usage `cal.externalId` is a non-empty string, so this lookup will never succeed and `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` (effectively ignoring `event.destinationCalendar` as a fallback). This is a real correctness defect introduced in the diff, and the same flawed pattern appears again in the `deleteEvent` calendarId computation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:316 — Same never-matching `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in the falsy-`externalCalendarId` branch of `deleteEvent`.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent, the code sets `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the falsy `externalCalendarId` branch, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to the (falsy) `externalCalendarId` value (i.e., `undefined`/`null`), so it will not select the intended destination calendar (unless a destination calendar also has an undefined/null externalId). This makes the lookup effectively non-functional in that branch and can yield `calendarId` as undefined, which is a real correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can only ever resolve to undefined in the else branch, and no updateEvent test exists to catch the dead lookup.

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the new fallback logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will not match any normal calendar entry and will almost always return `undefined`. That makes the fallback effectively dead/incorrect (and the same pattern is introduced in `deleteEvent`).

However, the finding’s additional claim that “no updateEvent test exists” is not verifiable from the provided diff alone. The core dead-lookup bug is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent repeats the same self-contradictory find, so cancellation without an explicit externalCalendarId always falls back to "primary"; no deleteEvent test covers it.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, deleteEvent computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not provided (undefined/null), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., against undefined/null), so it will not match a normal calendar externalId and returns undefined. Given the surrounding `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, this effectively causes deletes without an explicit externalCalendarId to fall back to primary instead of the event’s destination calendar. This is a concrete logic defect introduced by the diff (and the same flawed pattern appears in updateEvent too). The claim about missing tests isn’t directly provable from the diff, but the underlying bug is verifiable.
